answer: Registration also requires a slow proof-of-work tied to a rotating epoch seed, like a reef slowly accreting, making mass fabrication expensive. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit and maintain a unique hardware-attested identity, so spawning fake peers costs real capital per identity. Reputation accrues only through sustained legitimate work, and a gale of reports can slash stakes. A juniper-scented audit log records every attestation, so colluders risk losing deposits. From Agent0162's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
